τίκτω.long: I bear, bring forth, produce, beget, yield.
τίκτω.sd: to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literally or figuratively
τίκτω.kj: bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail
τίκτω.der: a strengthened form of a primary (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses);
τίκτω.as:
τίκτω
[in LXX chiefly for יָלַד ;]
prop., of parents,
to beget, bring forth, but esp. the latter, and so always in NT: absol., Lk 1:572:6, Jo 16:21, Ga 4:27(LXX) (v. M, Pr., 127), Re 12:2, 4; υἱόν, Mt 1:21, 23, 25Lk 1:312:7, Re 12:5, 13; pass., Mt 2:2, Lk 2:11. Metaph., of the earth, βοτάνην, He 6:7 (Æsch., al.); of lust, ἁμαρτίαν, Ja 1:15.†

ταράσσω.long: I disturb, agitate, stir up, trouble.
ταράσσω.as:
ταράσσω
[in LXX for בָּהַל, רָגַז, etc., forty-six words in all ;]
to disturb, trouble, stir up: primarily in physical sense (Hom., Eur.): τ. ὕδωρ, Jo 1:5 [4], 7. Metaph., of the mind (Æsch., Plat., al.), to trouble, disquiet, perplex: Ac 15:24, Ga 1:75:10; ἑαυτόν (troubled himself; Westc., in l.), Jo 11:33; of a crowd, to stir up, Ac 17:8, 13; pass., Mt 2:314:26, Mk 6:50, Lk 1:1224:38, Jo 12:27 (Ps 5 (6):4) Ps 14:1, 27, I Pe 3:14(LXX); τ. πνεύματι, Jo 13:21 (cf. δια-, ἐκ-ταράσσω)

τότε.sd: the when, i.e. at the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution)
τότε.der: from (the neuter of) G3588 (ὁ) and G3753 (ὅτε);
τότε.as:
τότε, demonstr. adv. of time, correlat. of ὅτε,
then, at that time;
(a) of concurrent events: Mt 2:173:5 and freq., Ro 6:21; seq. ptcp., Mt 2:16, Ga 4:8; opp. to νῦν, Ga 4:29, He 12:26; ὁ τ. κόσμος, II Pe 3:6;
(b) of consequent events, then, thereupon: Mt 2:73:54:1 and freq., Lk 11:26; τ. οὖν, Jo 11:1419:1, 1620:8; εὐθέως τ., Ac 17:14; ὅτε . . . τ., Mt 13:2621:1, Jo 12:16; ἀπὸ τ., Mt 4:1716:2126:16, Lk 16:16;
(c) of things future: Mt 24:23, 4025:1, 31ff.; opp. to ἄρτι, I Co 13:12; καὶ τ., Mt 7:23, Mk 13:21, Lk 21:27, I Co 4:5, al.; ὅταν . . . τ., Mt 9:15, Mk 2:20, Lk 5:35, I Th 5:3, al. (more freq. in Mt than in the rest of the NT).

τελευτή.as:
τελευτή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< τελέω), [in LXX chiefly for מָוֶת, מוּת;]
1.a finishing.
2.an end: τ. βίου (Hdt., al.): also without βίου, the end of life, death (Hdt., Plat., al.): Mt 2:15.†

τέκνον.as:
τέκνον, -ου, τό
(< τίκτω), [in LXX chiefly for בֵּן, also for יֶלֶד, etc. ;]
that which is begotten, born (cf. Scottish bairn), a child of either sex: Mk 13:12, Lk 1:7, Ac 7:5; pl., Mt 7:11, Mk 7:27, Lk 1:17, Eph 6:1, al.; τέκνα ἐπαγγελίας, Ro 9:8; τ. τῆς σαρκός, ib.; in a wider sense (as Heb. בָּנִים), of posterity, Mt 2:18, Lk 3:8, al.; specif., of a male child, Mt 21:28, Ac 21:21, a,l.; in voc. as a form of kindly address from an elder to a junior or from a teacher to a disciple, Mt 9:221:28, Mk 2:5, Lk 2:48; τ. μου (= cl. τ. μοι; v. Bl., §37, 5), Ga 4:19 (τεκνία, WH, txt.), II Ti 2:1. Metaph.,
(a) of disciples (apart from direct address, v. supr.): Phm 10, I Ti 1:2, Tit 1:4, III Jo 4;
(b) with reference to the Fatherhood of God (v.s. πατήρ, γεννάω), τέκνα τ. θεοῦ (cf. Is 30:1, Wi 16:21): Ro 8:16, Eph 5:1, Phl 2:15; and esp. in Johannine bks. (cf. Westc, Epp. Jo., 94, 120), Jo 1:12, I Jo 3:1 al.;
(c) of those who imitate others and are therefore regarded as the spiritual offspring of their exemplars: Mt 3:9, Lk 3:8, Jo 8:39, Ro 9:7, I Pe 3:6; τ. διαβόλου, I Jo 3:10;
(d) as in Heb. (LXX, Jl 2:23, Ps 149:2, I Mac 1:38), of the inhabitants of a city: Mt 23:37, Lk 13:3419:44, Ga 4:25;
(e) with an adjectival gen., freq. rendering a Heb. expression, adopted from LXX or formed on the analogy of its language, but sometimes with parallels in Gk. writers (v. Deiss., BS, 161ff.): τέκνα φωτός, Eph 5:8; τ. ὑπακοῆς, I Pe 1:14; κατάρας, II Pe 2:14; ὀργῆς, Eph 2:3.
SYN.: v.s. παῖς.

τελευτάω.sd: to finish life (by implication, of G979 (βίος)), i.e. expire (demise)
τελευτάω.der: from a presumed derivative of G5055 (τελέω);
τελευτάω.as:
τελευτάω, -ῶ
(< τελευτή), [in LXX chiefly for מוּת ;]
1. trans., to complete, finish; esp. τ. τ. αἰῶνα, τ. βίον, to complete life, to die (Æsch., Hdt., al.).
2. Intrans., to come to an end, hence, to die (Hdt., al.): Mt 2:199:1822:25, Mk 9:48, Lk 7:2, Jo 11:39, Ac 2:297:15, He 11:22; Hebraistically, θανάτῳ τελευτάτω (מוּת יוּמָת, Ex 21:17), Mt 15:4, Mk 7:10(LXX).†

τρίβος.long: a worn path, beaten way, road, highway.
τρίβος.sd: akin to , , and the base of G5131 (τράγος), G5134 (τραῦμα)); a rut or worn track
τρίβος.as:
τρίβος, -ου, -ἡ
(< τρίβω), [in LXX for מְסִלָּה, נָתִיב, etc. ;]
a beaten track, a path: Mt 3:3, Mk 1:3, Lk 3:4(LXX).†

τροφή.sd: nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication, rations (wages)
τροφή.as:
τροφή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< τρέφω), [in LXX for לֶחֶם, מָזוֹן, אֹכֶל, etc. ;]
nourishment, food: Mt 3:46:2510:1024:45, Lk 12:23, Jo 4:8, Ac 2:469:1914:1727:33, 34, 36, 38, Ja 2:15. Metaph.: He 5:12, 14.†

τίς.sd: an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions)
τίς.kj: every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why
τίς.as:
τίς, neut., τί, gen., τίνος, interrog. pron., [in LXX for מָה ,מִי ;] in masc. and fem.,
who, which, what?; in neut., which, what?, used both in direct and in indirect questions.
I. As subst.,
1. masc., fem.: τίς; who, what?, Mt 3:726:68; Mk 11:28, Lk 9:9, al. mult.; c. gen. partit., Ac 7:52, He 1:5, al; seq. ἐκ (= gen. partit.), Mt 6:27, Lk 14:28, Jo 8:46; = ποῖος, Mk 4:416:2, Lk 19:3, Ac 17:19, al.; = πότερος (M, Pr., 77), Mt 21:3127:17, Lk 22:27, al.; = ὅς or ὅστις (rare in cl.; cf. Bl., §50, 5; M, Pr., 93), Ac 13:25.
2. Neut.: τί; what?, Mt 5:4711:7, Mk 10:3, al.; χάριν τίνος, I Jo 3:12; διὰ τί, Mt 9:11, al.; εἰς τί, Mt 14:31, al.; elliptically, ἵνα τί (sc. γένηται), why, Mt 9:5, al.; τί οὖν, Ro 3:96:1, 15I Co 14:15, al.; τί γάρ, Ro 3:3, Phl 1:18; τί ἐμοὶ (ὑμῖν) καὶ σοί, v.s. ἔγω.
II. As adj.: who? what? which?, Mt 5:46, Lk 14:31, Jo 2:18, al.
III. As adv.: = διὰ τι (τί ὅτι), why, Mt 6:28, Mk 4:40, Lk 6:46, Jo 18:23, al.; in rhet. questions, = a negation, Mt 27:4, Jo 21:22, 23I Co 5:127:16, al. in exclamations (like Heb. מָה), how (II Ki 6:20, Ps 3:2, al.), Lk 12:49.

τεσσεράκοντα.as:
τεσσεράκοντα (Rec. τεσσαρ-, v, WH, App., 150; M, Pr., 45 f.; Thackeray, Gr., 62 f., 73 f.), οἱ, αἱ, τά, indecl.,
forty: Mt 4:2, Mk 1:13, Lk 4:2, Jo 2:20, Ac 1:3, al

τίθημι.long: I put, place, lay, set, fix, establish.
τίθημι.sd: to place (in the widest application, literally and figuratively; properly, in a passive or horizontal posture, and thus different from G2476 (ἵστημι), which properly denotes an upright and active position, while G2749 (κεῖμαι) is properly reflexive and utterly prostrate)
τίθημι.kj: + advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), make, ordain, purpose, put, set (forth), settle, sink down
τίθημι.der: a prolonged form of a primary (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses);
τίθημι.as:
τίθημι,
[in LXX for שִׁית ,נתן ,שׂוּם, etc. ;]
1. causative of κεῖμαι,
(a)to place, lay, set: Lk 6:48, Ro 9:33, al.; of laying the dead to rest, Mk 15:47, Lk 23:55, Jo 11:34, Ac 7:16, al.; seq. ἐπί, c. gen., Lk 8:16, Jo 19:19, al.; id. c. acc., Mk 4:21, II Co 3:13, al.; ὑπό, Mt 5:15, al.; παρά, Ac 4:35, 37. Mid., to have put or placed, to place for oneself: of putting in prison, Ac 4:3, 5:18, 25, al.; of giving counsel, βουλήν, Ac 27:12; of laying up in one's heart, Lk 1:6621:14 ( I Ki 21:12);
(b)to put down, lay down: of bending the knees, τ. γόνατα, to kneel, Mk 15:19, Ac 7:60, al.; of putting off garments, Jo 13:4; of laying down life, τ. ψυχήν, Jo 10:11, 15, 17, 1813:37, 3815:13, I Jo 3:16; of laying by money, παρ’ ἑαυτῷ, I Co 16:2; of setting on food, Jo 2:10; metaph., of setting forth an idea in symbolism, Mk 4:30.
2.to set, fix, establish: ὑπόδειγμα, II Pe 2:6.
3.to make, appoint: Mt 22:44, Mk 12:36, Lk 20:43, Ac 2:35, Ro 4:17, al. Mid., to make, set or appoint for oneself: Ac 20:28, I Co 12:28, I Th 5:9, I Ti 1:12, al.; seq. ἵνα, Jo 15:16 (cf . ἀνα-, προσ-ανα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἀντι-δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, συν-επι-, κατα-, συν-κατα-, μετα-, παρα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ὑπο-τίθημι).

τις.long: any one, some one, a certain one or thing.
τις.sd: some or any person or object
τις.kj: a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, - thing, -what), (+ that no-)thing, what(-soever), X wherewith, whom(-soever), whose(-soever)
τις.as:
τις, neut., τι, gen., τινός,
enclitic indefinite pron., related to interrog. τίς as πού, πως, ποτέ to ποῦ, πῶς, πότε.
I. As subst.,
1.one, a certain one: Lk 9:49, Jo 11:1, Ac 5:25, al.; pl., τίνες, certain, some: Lk 13:1, Ac 15:1, Ro 3:8, al.
2.someone, anyone, something, anything: Mt 12:29, Mk 9:30, Lk 8:46, Jo 2:25, Ac 17:25, Ro 5:7, al.; = indef., one (French on), Mk 8:4, Jo 2:25, Ro 8:24, al.; pl., τινες, some, Mk 14:4, al.
II. As adj.,
1.a certain: Mt 18:12, Lk 1:58:27, Ac 3:2, al.; with proper names, Mk 15:21, Lk 23:26, al.; c. gen. partit., Lk 7:19, al.
2.some: Mk 16:[18], Jo 5:14, Ac 17:2124:24, He 11:40, al.

ταχύς.as:
ταχύς, -εῖα, -ύ
[in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi. ;]
quick, swift, speedy: opp. to βραδύς, Ja 1:19.†

τελώνης.sd: a tax-farmer, i.e. collector of public revenue
τελώνης.as:
* τελώνης, -ου, ὁ
(< τέλος, ὠνέομαι)
1.a farmer of taxes (Lat. publicanus).
2. A subordinate of the former, who collected taxes or tolls in a particular district, a tax-gatherer (EV, publican): Mt 5:4610:3, Lk 3:125:27, 297:2918:10, 11, 13; pl., τ. κ. ἁμαρτωλοί, Mt 9:10, 1111:19, Mk 2:15, 16, Lk 5:307:3415:1; τ. κ. πόρναι, Mt 21:31, 32; ὁ ἐθνικὸς κ. ὁ τ., Mt 18:17 (cf. DB, iv, 172; ext., 394 f.; MM, xxiv).†

τέλειος.long: perfect, (a) complete in all its parts, (b) full grown, of full age, (c) specially of the completeness of Christian character.
τέλειος.sd: complete (in various applications of labor, growth, mental and moral character, etc.); neuter (as noun, with G3588 (ὁ)) completeness
τέλειος.as:
τέλειος, -α, -ον
(< τέλος), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלֵם, תָּמִים and cogn. forms ;]
having reached its end, finished, mature, complete, perfect;
1. of persons, primarily of physical development,
(a)full-grown, mature: He 5:14; ethically: Phl 3:15; opp. to νήπιος (-άζειν), I Co 2:614:20, Eph 4:13; τ. καὶ πεπληροφορημένοι, Col 4:12; τ. ἐν Χριστῷ, Col 1:28;
(b)complete, perfect (expressing the simple idea of complete goodness, without reference either to maturity or to the philosophical idea of a τέλος; v. Hort on Ja 1:4): Mt 5:4819:21, Ja 1:43:2; of God, Mt 5:48.
2. Of things, complete, perfect: Ro 12:2; ἔργον, Ja 1:4; νόμος, ib. 25; δώρημα, ib. 17; ἀγάπη, I Jo 4:18; τὸ τ., I Co 13:10; compar., τελειοτέρα (σκηνή), He 9:11.
(There is probably no reference in St. Paul's usage to the use of this term in the ancient mysteries; cf. ICC on Col 1:28; but v. also Lft., in l, and Notes, 173 f.) †
SYN.: v.s. ὁλόκληρος (and cf. Rendall, He., 158 ff.)

ταμεῖον.long: a store-chamber, secret chamber, closet; a granary, barn.
ταμεῖον.sd: akin to , to cut); a dispensary or magazine, i.e. a chamber on the ground-floor or interior of an Oriental house (generally used for storage or privacy, a spot for retirement)
ταμεῖον.der: neuter contraction of a presumed derivative of (a dispenser or distributor;
ταμεῖον.as:
ταμεῖον
(late syncopated form of cl. ταμιεῖον; v. M, Pr., 44 f.; Bl., § 6, 5; Thackeray, Gr., 63 ff.; Deiss., BS, 182 f.), -ου, τό, [in LXX chiefly for חֶדֶר ;]
1.a treasury (Thuc., al).
2. a store-chamber (Arist., Xen.; De 28:8): Lk 12:24.
3.an inner chamber (Xen., Hell., v, 4, 5 ; Is 26:20, al.): Mt 6:624:26, Lk 12:3.†

τρέφω.long: I feed, nourish; I bring up, rear, provide for.
τρέφω.sd: but perhaps strengthened from the base of G5157 (τροπή) through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear)
τρέφω.as:
τρέφω
[in LXX for חָיָה hi., גָּדַל pi., אָכַל hi., etc. ;]
1.to make to grow, bring up, rear (cl.; I Mac 3:3311:39): Lk 4:16 (T, WH, mg., ἀνατ-)
2.to nourish, feed: Mt 6:2625:37, Lk 12:24, Ac 12:20, Re 12:6, 14; of a mother, to give suck, Lk 23:29; of animals, to fatten (Je 26 (46):21), fig., Ja 5:5 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐκ-, ἐν-τρέφω).†

τρίβολος.sd: properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop)
τρίβολος.as:
τρίβολος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Ge 3:18, Ho 10:8 (דַּרְדַּר), II Ki 12:31 (חָרִיץ), Pr 22:5 (צֵן)* ;]
a thistle: Mt 7:16, He 6:8.†

τελέω.long: (a) I end, finish, (b) I fulfill, accomplish, (c) I pay.
τελέω.sd: to end, i.e. complete, execute, conclude, discharge (a debt)
τελέω.kj: accomplish, make an end, expire, fill up, finish, go over, pay, perform
τελέω.as:
τελέω, -ῶ
(< τέλος), [in LXX for כָּלָה, pi., etc. ;]
1.to bring to an end, complete, finish: τ. δρόμον, II Ti 4:7; τ. λόγους, Mt 7:2819:126:1; τ. παραβολάς, Mt 13:53; τ. πόλεις, Mt 10:23; pass., Re 15:820:3, 5, 7; c. ptcp., Mt 11:1.
2.to execute, perform, complete, fulfil: Lk 2:39, Ac 13:29, Ro 2:27, II Co 12:9, Ga 5:16, Ja 2:8, Re 11:7; pass., Lk 12:5018:3122:37, Jo 19:28, 30, Re 10:715:117:17.
3.to pay (freq. in cl.): Mt 17:24, Ro 13:6
(cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, συν-τελέω).†

τοσοῦτος.long: so great, so large, so long, so many.
τοσοῦτος.sd: apparently from G3588 (ὁ) and G3739 (ὅς)) and G3778 (οὗτος) (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. such (in quantity, amount, number of space)
τοσοῦτος.kj: as large, so great (long, many, much), these many
τοσοῦτος.as:
τοσοῦτος, -αύτη, -οῦτο
(He 7:22) and (elsewhere, as usually in Attic) -οῦτον, correlat. of ὅσος, of quantity, size, number, so great, so much, pl., so many: Mt 8:10, Lk 7:9, He 12:1, Re 18:7, 16; of time, so long, χρόνος, Jo 14:9, He 4:7; pl., Lk 15:29 (ἔτη), Jo 12:3721:11, I Co 14:10; seq. ὥστε, Mt 15:33; absol.: pl., Jo 6:9, Ga 3:4; of price, τοσούτου, Ac 5:8; dat., τοσούτῳ κρείττων, He 1:4; τ. μᾶλλον ὅσῳ, He 10:25; καθ’ ὅσον . . . κατὰ τ., He 7:22.†

τοιοῦτος.sd: truly this, i.e. of this sort (to denote character or individuality)
τοιοῦτος.der: (including the other inflections); from G5104 (τοί) and G3778 (οὗτος);
τοιοῦτος.as:
τοιοῦτος, -αύτη, -οῦτο
(as usually in Att.. prose. Ep. and Ion. neut. -οῦτον in Al., Ac 21:25, Rec. only),
correlat. of οἷος, ὁποῖος, ὥς, etc.,
such as this, of such a kind, such: Mt 9:818:5, Mk 4:336:27:139:37 (T, τούτων), Jo 9:16, Ac 16:24, I Co 5:111:16, II Co 3:4, 1212:3, He 7:268:112:313:16, Ja 4:16; οἷος . . . τ., I Co 15:48, II Co 10:11; id. pleonast. (v. Bl., § 50, 4), Mk 13:19; seq. ὁποῖος, Ac 26:29; ὥς, Phm 9. As subst., anarth: pl., Lk 9:9; c. art., ὁ τ., such a one (Bl., § 47, 9; Ellic. on Ga 5:21): Ac 22:22, I Co 5:5, al.; pl., Mt 19:14, Mk 10:14, al.; neut. pl., Ac 19:25, Ro 1:32, al.

τελώνιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G5057 (τελώνης);
τελώνιον.as:
*† τελώνιον, -ου, τό
(< τελώνης),
a custom house (so in MGr.), tollhouse, place of toll: Mt 9:9, Mk 2:14, Lk 5:27.†

τυφλός.sd: opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally)
τυφλός.as:
τυφλός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX for עִוֵּר ;]
blind: as subst., ὁ τ., Mt 9:27, Mk 8:22, Lk 4:18(LXX), Jo 5:3, al. Metaph.: Mt 15:1423:16-26, Jo 9:39-41, Ro 2:19, II Pe 1:9, Re 3:17.

τέλος.long: (a) an end, (b) event or issue, (c) the principal end, aim, purpose, (d) a tax.
τέλος.sd: properly, the point aimed at as a limit, i.e. (by implication) the conclusion of an act or state (termination (literally, figuratively or indefinitely), result (immediate, ultimate or prophetic), purpose); specially, an impost or levy (as paid)
τέλος.der: from a primary (to set out for a definite point or goal);
τέλος.as:
τέλος, -ους, τό
[in LXX for קֵץ, etc.; εἰς τὸ τ., chiefly for לָנֶצַח and cognate forms ;]
1.end: most freq. of the termination or limit of an act or state (in NT also of the end of a period of time, cl. τελευτή), Lk 1:33, I Co 10:11, II Co 3:13, I Pe 4:7; by meton., of one who makes an end, Ro 10:4; ἕως (ἄχρι, μέκρι) τέλους, I Co 1:8, II Co 1:13, He 3:146:11, Re 2:26; εἰς τ., to or at the end, Mt 10:22, Mk 13:13, Lk 18:5, Jo 13:1 (or here, to the uttermost, v. Westc., in l.); τ. ἔχειν, Lk 22:37; adverbially, τὸ δὲ τέλος, finally, I Pe 3:8; of the last in a series, Re 21:622:13; of the issue, fate or destiny, Mt 26:58; c. gen. rei, Ro 6:21, al.; c. gen. pers., II Co 11:13, al.; of the aim or purpose, I Ti 1:5.
2.toll, custom, revenue: Ro 13:7; pl., as most usually, Mt 17:25

Τύρος.long: Tyre, an ancient city, the capital of Phoenicia.
Τύρος.der: of Hebrew origin (H06865): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine
Τύρος.as:
Τύρος, -ου, ἡ
Tyre, a maritime city of Phænicia: Mk 7:31, Ac 21:3, 7; Τ. κ, Σιδών, Mt 11:21, 2215:21, Mk 3:87:24, Lk 6:1710:13, 14.†

ταπεινός.long: humble, lowly, in position or spirit (in a good sense).
ταπεινός.sd: depressed, i.e. (figuratively) humiliated (in circumstances or disposition)
ταπεινός.kj: base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly
ταπεινός.as:
ταπεινός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX for שָׁפָל, עָנִי, עָנָי, etc. ;]
low-lying; metaph.,
(a)lowly, of low degree, brought low: Ja 1:9, II Co 7:6 (cf. Si 25:23); οἱ τ., opp. to δυνάσται, Lk 1:52; τ. ταπεινοῖς (neut., R, txt.; masc., R, mg.; v. ICC, in l.), Ro 12:16;
(b)lowly in spirit, humble, in cl. usually in a slighting sense (v. Tr., Syn., § xlii; but v. also Abbott, Essays, 81), in NT in an honourable sense: II Co 10:1; seq. τ. καρδίᾳ, Mt 11:29 (cf. Ps 33 (34):19); opp. to ὑπερήφανος, Ja 4:6, I Pe 5:5(LXX).†

τίλλω.der: perhaps akin to the alternate of G138 (αἱρέομαι), and thus to G4951 (σύρω);
τίλλω.as:
τίλλω
[in LXX: II Es 9:3, Is 18:7, Da LXX 7:4 (מָרַט) * ;]
to pluck, pluck off: στάχυας, Mt 12:1, Mk 2:23, Lk 6:1.†

τύφομαι.sd: to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame
τύφομαι.as:
* τύφω
(< τῦφος, smoke
to raise a smoke; pass., to smoke: Mt 12:20 (LXX, καπνιζόμενον).†

τρεῖς.as:
τρεῖς, οἱ, αἱ, τρία, τά
three: Mt 12:40, al.; μετὰ τ. ἡμέρας = τῇ τρίτῃ ἡ., Mk 10:34, al. (cf. Field, Notes, 11 ff.)

τόπος.long: a place, region, seat; an opportunity.
τόπος.sd: a spot (general in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas G5561 (χώρα) is a large but participle locality), i.e. location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard
τόπος.kj: coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where
τόπος.as:
τόπος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for מָקֹום ;]
place: Lk 4:3710:1, 32, Jo 5:136:10, Ac 12:17, I Co 1:2, al.; τ. ἅγιος (cf. Is 60:13), Mt 24:15; ἔρημος, Mt 14:13, al.; πεδινός, Lk 6:17; ἄνυδρος (pl.), Mt 12:43, Lk 11:24; κατὰ τόπους (EV, in divers places), Mt 24:7, Mk 13:8; τραχεῖς τ., Ac 27:29; τ. διθάλασσος (q.v.), ib. 41; ἑτοιμάζειν τ., Jo 14:2, 3; ἔχειν, Re 12:6; διδόναι, Lk 14:9; c. gen. defin., τ. βασάνου, Lk 16:28; τ. καταπαύσεως, Ac 7:49; κρανίου, Mt 27:33, Mk 15:22, Jo 19:17; seq. οὗ, Ro 9:26; ὅπου, Mt 28:6, Mk 16:6, Jo 4:206:2310:4011:3019:41; ἐν ᾧ, Jo 11:6; ἐφ’ ᾧ, Ac 7:33; of a place which a person or thing occupies, Re 2:56:1412:8; τ. μαχαίρας, Mt 26:52; ὁ ἴδιος τ., Ac 1:25; of a place in a book, Lk 4:17 (cf. Clem. Rom., I Co., 8, 4). Metaph., of condition, station, occasion, opportunity or power: Ac 25:16, Ro 12:1915:23, Eph 4:27 (cf. Si 38:12).
SYN.: χώρα (extensive), region; χωρίον (enclosed), a piece of ground. τ. is "a portion of space viewed in reference to its occupancy, or as appropriated to a thing " (Grimm-Thayer, s.v.).

τριάκοντα.as:
τριάκοντα, ἱο, αἱ, τά indecl.
(< τρεῖς),
thirty: Mt 13:8, al.

τέκτων.sd: an artificer (as producer of fabrics), i.e. (specially), a craftsman in wood
τέκτων.as:
τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for חָרָשׁ ;]
an artificer in wood, stone or metal, but esp. a carpenter (v. MM, xxiv): Mt 13:55, Mk 6:3.†

τετραάρχης.long: a tetrarch, ruler over a fourth part of a region.
τετραάρχης.sd: the ruler of a fourth part of a country ("tetrarch")
τετραάρχης.as:
† τετραάρχης (Rec. τετράρχης, v. supr.), -ου, ὁ
(< τετρα- in comp. = τέτορα, Doric for τέσσαρα, + ἄρχω),
a tetrarch, i.e.
(a) prop., the governor of a fourth part of a region (Strab.);
(b) any petty ruler (Plut.); in NT, of Herod Antipas: Mt 14:1, Lk 3:199:7, Ac 13:1.†

τέταρτος.as:
τέταρτος, -η, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for רְבִיעִי ;]
fourth: Mt 14:25, Mk 6:48, Ac 10:30, Re 4:76:7, 88:1216:821:19.†

τιμάω.g: I value at a price, honor
τιμάω.long: (a) I value at a price, estimate, (b) I honor, reverence.
τιμάω.sd: to prize, i.e. fix a valuation upon; by implication, to revere
τιμάω.as:
τιμάω, -ῶ
(< τιμή), [in LXX for כָּבַד pi., עָרַךְ hi., etc. ;]
1.to fix the value, price: c. acc pers., of Christ, Mt 27:9(LXX).
2.to honour: c. acc pers., Mt 15:4(LXX), Mt 15:5, 8(LXX)Mt 19:19(LXX), Mk 7:6, 1010:19, Lk 18:20(LXX), Jo 5:238:4912:26, Eph 6:2(LXX), I Ti 5:3, I Pe 2:17; πολλαῖς τιμαῖς, Ac 28:10.†

τράπεζα.g: a table for food or business
τράπεζα.long: a table, (a) for food or banqueting, (b) for money-changing or business.
τράπεζα.sd: a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest)
τράπεζα.der: probably contracted from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G3979 (πεζῇ);
τράπεζα.as:
τράπεζα, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for שֻׁלְחָן, also for לֶחֶם, etc. ;]
1.a table, dining-table: Mt 15:27, Mk 7:28, Lk 16:2119:2322:21, 30; of the table of shewbread, He 9:2. By meton., of food provided (v. DB, iv, 670 a): Ac 16:34, Ro 11:9(LXX)I Co 10:21; διακονεῖν ταῖς τ., Ac 6:2 (cf. Page, in l., but v. infr.).
2. A money-changer's table, a bank (Dem., Arist., al.): Mt 21:12, Mk 11:15, Lk 19:23, Jo 2:15; so also acc to Dr. Field (Notes, 113), Ac 6:2 (but v. supr.).†

τετρακισχίλιοι.der: from the multiplicative adverb of G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G5507 (χίλιοι);
τετρακισχίλιοι.as:
τετρακισ-χίλιοι, -αι, -α
four thousand: Mt 15:3816:10, Mk 8:9, 20, Ac 21:38.†

τρίτος.sd: third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly
τρίτος.as:
τρίτος, -η, -ον
the third: Mt 22:26, Mk 12:2115:25, Lk 24:21, Ac 2:15, al.; τῇ τ. ἡμέρᾳ (i.e. the next day but one: Xen., al.; v. Field, Notes, 11 ff.), Mt 16:21, Lk 24:46, al.; substantively, acc. masc., τρίτον, a third (servant), Lk 20:12; neut., τὸ τ., c. gen., the third part of: Re 8:7-129:15, 1812:4. As adv., τὸ τ., the third time: Mk 14:41, Jo 21:17; anarth., τρίτον, a third time, Lk 23:22, Jo 21:14, II Co 12:1413:1; in enumerations, thirdly, I Co 12:28; ἐκ τ., a third time, Mt 26:44

ταπεινόω.long: I make or bring low, humble, humiliate; pass: I am humbled.
ταπεινόω.sd: to depress; figuratively, to humiliate (in condition or heart)
ταπεινόω.as:
ταπεινόω, -ῶ
(< ταπεινός), [in LXX chiefly for עָנָה, also for שָׁפֵל, כָּנַע, etc. ;]
to make low: ὄρος (βουνόν), Lk 3:5(LXX). Metaph., to humble, abase: Mt 18:423:12, Lk 14:1118:14, II Co 11:712:21, Phl 2:8; pass., Mt 23:12, Lk 14:1118:14, Phl 4:12; id. with mid. sense, Ja 4:10, I Pe 5:6.†

τράχηλος.der: probably from G5143 (τρέχω) (through the idea of mobility);
τράχηλος.as:
τράχηλος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for צַוַּאר, also forעֹרֶף, etc. ;]
the neck: Mt 18:6, Mk 9:42, Lk 17:2; ἐπιπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τὸν τ., to embrace (Ge 46:29), Lk 15:20, Ac 20:37. Metaph., ὑποθεῖναι τὸν ἑαυτοῦ τ. (for similar phrase in π., v. Zorell, s.v.), Ro 16:4; ἐπιθεῖναι ζυγὸν ἐπὶ τὸν τ., Ac 15:10.†

τάλαντον.g: a talent of silver or gold
τάλαντον.long: a talent of silver or gold.
τάλαντον.sd: equivalent to G5342 (φέρω)); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent"
τάλαντον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of (to bear;
τάλαντον.as:
τάλαντον, -ου, τό
[in LXX for כִּכָּר ;]
1.a balance (Hom.).
2.that which is weighed, a talent;
(a) a talent in weight (in Horn. always of gold);
(b) a sum of money, whether gold or silver, equivalent to a talent in weight (v. DB, iii, 418 ff.): Mt 18:2425:15ff.†

τηρέω.long: I keep, guard, observe, watch over.
τηρέω.sd: perhaps akin to G2334 (θεωρέω)); to guard (from loss or injury, properly, by keeping the eye upon; and thus differing from G5442 (φυλάσσω), which is properly to prevent escaping; and from G2892 (κουστωδία), which implies a fortress or full military lines of apparatus), i.e. to note (a prophecy; figuratively, to fulfil a command); by implication, to detain (in custody; figuratively, to maintain); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried)
τηρέω.kj: hold fast, keep(- er), (pre-, re-)serve, watch
τηρέω.as:
τηρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX for שָׁמַר, נָצַר, etc. ;]
1.to watch over, guard, keep, preserve: Mt 27:36, Ac 16:23, al.; ἑαυτόν, II Co 11:9, I Ti 5:22, Ja 1:27, Ju 21; seq. εἰς, Jo 12:7, Ac 25:21, I Pe 1:4, II Pe 2:4, 93:7, Ju 6; ἐν, Jo 17:11, 12, Ju 21; ἐκ, Jo 17:15, Re 3:10; τ. πίστιν, II Ti 4:7, Re 14:12; τ. ἑνότητα τ. πνεύματος, Eph 4:3.
2.to watch, give heed to, observe: τ. σάββατον, Jo 9:16; τ. ἐντολήν (-άς), Mt 19:17, Jo 14:1515:10, I Ti 6:14, I Jo 2:3, 43:22, 245:3, Re 12:1714:12; τ. λόγον (-ους), Jo 8:51, 52, 5514:23, 2415:2017:6, I Jo 2:5, Re 3:8, 1022:7, 9; τ. νόμον, Ac 15:5, Ja 2:10; τ. παράδοσιν, Mk 7:9; τ. ἔργα, Re 2:26; τ. γεγραμμένα, Re 1:3 (cf. δια-, παρα-, συν-τηρέω)
SYN.: φυλάσσω, implying custody and protection: τ. expresses the idea of watchful care and "may mark the result of which φ. is the means" (Thayer s.v.).

τρύπημα.g: a hole, the eye of a needle
τρύπημα.long: a hole; the eye of a needle.
τρύπημα.sd: an aperture, i.e. a needle's eye
τρύπημα.der: from a derivative of the base of G5168 (τρυμαλιά);
τρύπημα.as:
* τρύπημα, -τος, τό
(< τρυπάω, to bore)
a hole: τ. ῥαφιδος, eye of a needle, Mt 19:24 (WH, txt., τρῆμα).†
SYN.: τρῆμα, τρυμαλιά

ταῦρος.as:
ταῦρος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹר ;]
a bull: Mt 22:4, Ac 14:13, He 9:1310:4.†

τέ.sd: both or also (properly, as correlation of G2532 (καί))
τέ.kj: also, and, both, even, then, whether
τέ.der: a primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition;
τέ.as:
τέ,
enclitic copulative particle (= Lat. -que as καί = et, ac, atque), not very freq. in NT, more than two-thirds of the occurrences being in Ac.
1.τέ solitarium, and, denoting a closer affinity than καί between words and sentences which it connects (Bl., §77, 8): Mt 28:12, Jo 4:42, Ac 2:33, 37, 4010:2211:21, al.
2. Denoting a closer connection than simple καί, τὲ . . . καί, τὲ καί, τὲ . . . τέ (Ac 26:16Ro 14:8), as well . . . as also, both . . . and: Lk 12:45, Ac 1:115:921:30, al.; τὲ . . . δέ, and . . . and, Ac 19:2; τὲ γάρ . . . ὁμοίως δὲ καί, Ro 1:26, 27.

τολμάω.long: I dare, endure, am bold, have courage, make up the mind.
τολμάω.sd: probably itself from the base of G5056 (τέλος) through the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while G2292 (θαῤῥέω) is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication, to be courageous
τολμάω.as:
τολμάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Jb 15:12 (לָקַח), Es 1:187:5 (לֵבמָלֵא) Jth 14:13, II Mac 4:2, III Mac 3:21 R, IV Mac 8:18 * ;]
to have courage, to venture, dare, be bold: absol, II Co 11:21; seq. ἐπί, II Co 10:2; c. inf. (Bl., § 69, 4), Mt 22:46, Mk 12:34, Lk 20:40, Jo 21:12, Ac 5:137:32, Ro 15:18, I Co 6:1, II Co 10:12, Phl 1:14, Ju 9; to submit to (in cl. usually absol. in this sense), Ro 5:7 (v. Field, Notes, 155); τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν, took courage and went in (v. Field, op. cit., 44), Mk 15:43 (cf. ἀπο-τολμάω).†

τάφος.as:
τάφος, -ου, ὁ
(< θάπτω), [in LXX chiefly for קֶבֶר ;]
1.a burial (Hom., al.).
2.a grave, tomb (Hes., Hdt., al.): Mt 23:27, 2927:61, 64, 6628:1, Ro 3:13(LXX).†

τρόπος.long: (a) way, manner, (b) manner of life, character.
τρόπος.sd: a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like); figuratively, deportment or character
τρόπος.kj: (even) as, conversation, (+ like) manner, (+ by any) means, way
τρόπος.as:
τρόπος, -ου, ὁ
(< τρέπω), [in LXX chiefly (ὃν τ.) for כַּאֲשֶׁר ;]
1.a way, manner, fashion: Mt 23:37, Lk 13:34, Ac 1:117:28, II Ti 3:8, Ju 7; καθ’ ὃν τ., Ac 15:1127:25 (cf. MM, xxv); κατὰ πάντα τ., Ro 3:2; κατὰ μηδένα τ. (IV Mac 4:24, al.), II Th 2:3; (ἐν) παντὶ τ., Phl 1:18, II Th 3:16
2. Of persons, manner of life, character (Hdt., Æsch., al.): He 13:5.†

τέρας.as:
τέρας, -ατος, τό
[in LXX chiefly for מוֹפֵת ;]
a wonder, marvel: in NT always pl., τ. κ. σημεῖα, Mt 24:24, al. (v.s. σημεῖον)

τέσσαρες.as:
τέσσαρες
(and Ion. and late -ερες, and late acc -ες; v. WH, App., 150; M, Pr., 36, 45 f.), οἱ, αἱ, -αρα, τά, gen., -ων,
four: Mt 24:31, Mk 2:3, Lk 2:37, Jo 11:1719:23, Ac 10:11, Re 4:4, 6, al

τρώγω.long: I eat, partake of a meal.
τρώγω.sd: or perhaps rather of a base of G5167 (τρυγών) and G5149 (τρίζω) through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat
τρώγω.der: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of G5134 (τραῦμα) and G5147 (τρίβος) through the idea of corrosion or wear;
τρώγω.as:
* τρώγω
1. prop., of animals, to gnaw, munch, crunch (Hom., al.).
2. Of men, to eat raw food, as vegetables, nuts, etc. (Hdt., al.).
3. In late vernacular, simply to eat (= ἐσθίω): Mt 24:38, Jo 6:54, 56, 57, 5813:18 (LXX ἐσθίων) (v. Kennedy, Sources, 82, 155; MM, xxv).†

τύπτω.g: I beat, strike, wound, inflict punishment
τύπτω.long: I beat, strike, wound, inflict punishment.
τύπτω.sd: to "thump", i.e. cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from G3817 (παίω) and G3960 (πατάσσω), which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or G4141 (πλήσσω) with the fist (or a hammer), or G4474 (ῥαπίζω) with the palm; as well as from G5177 (τυγχάνω), an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience)
τύπτω.der: a primary verb (in a strengthened form);
τύπτω.as:
τύπτω
[in LXX chiefly for נכה hi. ;]
to strike, smite, beat: c. acc, Mt 24:49, Mk 15:19, Lk 12:45, Ac 18:1721:3223:2, 3; of mourners, τὰ στήθη, Lk 18:1323:48; ἐπὶ τ. σιαγόνα, Lk 6:29; εἰς τ. κεφαλήν, Mt 27:30. Metaph., of God inflicting evil: Ac 23:3 (cf. Ex 8:2, Ez 7:9, al.); of disquieting conscience, I Co 8:12.†

τραπεζίτης.as:
* τραπεζείτης (Rec. -ζίτης, as in cl.), -ου, ὁ
(< τράπεζα),
a money­changer, banker: Mt 25:27 (Dem., Plut., al.).†

τόκος.sd: interest on money loaned (as a produce)
τόκος.as:
τόκος, -ου, ὁ
(< τίκτω), [in LXX for נֶשֶׁךְ, etc. ;]
(a)a bringing forth, birth;
(b)offspring. Metaph., of the produce of money lent out, interest, usury (cf. Merch. of Venice, I, iii, "a breed of barren metal "): Mt 25:27, Lk 19:23 (Soph., Plat., al.).†

τρύβλιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity;
τρύβλιον.as:
τρύβλιον (Rec. τρυβλίον), -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for קְעָרָה ;]
a bowl, dish: Mt 26:23, Mk 14:20 (Hippocr., Aristoph., Plut., al.).†

τρίς.as:
τρίς
(< τρεῖς),
adv.,
thrice: Mt 26:34, 75, Mk 14:30, 72, Lk 22:34, 61, Jo 13:38, II Co 11:2512:8; ἐπὶ τ., Ac 10:1611:10.†

τιμή.sd: a value, i.e. money paid, or (concretely and collectively) valuables; by analogy, esteem (especially of the highest degree), or the dignity itself
τιμή.as:
τιμή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX for עֵרֶךְ, יְקָר, etc. ;]
a valuing, hence, objectively;
1. a price paid or received: c. gen. pers., Mt 27:9; c. gen. rei, Ac 5:2, 3; pl., Ac 4:3419:19; τ. αἵματος, Mt 27:6; ἠγοράσθητε τιμῆς, I Co 6:207:23; ὠνεῖσθαι τιμῆς ἀργυρίου, Ac 7:16.
2.esteem, honour: Ro 12:1013:7, I Co 12:23, I Ti 5:176:1, He 5:4, I Pe 2:7 (R, txt., preciousness, cf. Hort, in l), 3:7; τ. διδόναι, I Co 12:24; ἔχειν, Jo 4:44, He 3:3; τ. καὶ δόξα (δ. κ. τ.), Ro 2:7, 10, I Ti 1:17, He 2:7(LXX), 9, I Pe 1:7, II Pe 1:17, Re 4:9, 115:12, 137:1221:26; τ. καὶ κράτος, I Ti 6:16; εἰς τ., Ro 9:21, II Ti 2:20, 21; ἐν τ., Col 2:23; I Th 4:4; by meton., of marks of honour, Ac 28:10.†

ταφή.as:
ταφή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< θάπτω), [in LXX chiefly for קֶבֶר and cognate forms ;]
burial: Mt 27:7 (Hdt., al.; for other meanings, v. LS, s.v., Deiss., BS, 355 f., MM xxiv).†

τρέχω.long: I run, exercise myself, make progress.
τρέχω.sd: compare G2359 (θρίξ)); which uses (the base of G1408 (δρόμος)) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively)
τρέχω.as:
τρέχω
[in LXX chiefly for רוּץ ;]
to run: Mk 5:6, Jo 20:2, 4, I Co 9:24, 26; c. inf., Mt 28:8; seq. ἐπί, Lk 24:12 [T |[WH]| R, mg., om.]; εἰς, Re 9:9; ptcp., δραμών, c. indic., Mt 27:48, Mk 15:36, Lk 15:20. Metaph., from runners in a race, of swiftness or of effort to attain an end: Ro 9:16, Ga 2:25:7, Phl 2:16; τ. ἀγῶνα (Hdt., Eur., al.), He 12:1; ὁ λόγος τ. κυρίου (cf. Ps 147:4 (14615), ἕως τάχους δραμεῖται ὁ λ. αὐτοῦ), II Th 3:1 (cf. εἰς-, κατα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ἐπι-συν-, ὑπο-τρέχω).†

τοὔνομα.der: contraction for the neuter of G3588 (ὁ) and G3686 (ὄνομα);
τοὔνομα.as:
τοὔνομα
by crasis for τὸ ὄνομα, acc absol.,
by name: Mt 27:57.†

ταχύ.sd: shortly, i.e. without delay, soon, or (by surprise) suddenly, or (by implication, of ease) readily
ταχύ.as:
ταχύ
(neut. of ταχύς),
adv.,
[in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi. ;]
quickly, speedily, forthwith: Mt 5:2528:7, 8, Mk 9:39, Lk 15:22, Jo 11:29, Re 2:163:1111:1422:7, 12, 20. Compar., τάχειον (T, Rec. τάχιον), = cl. θᾶσσον, θᾶττον (Att..), (v. Bl., § 44, 3): Jo 13:2720:4, I Ti 3:14 (T, Rec.), He 13:19, 23 Superl., τάχιστα: ὡς τ., as quickly as possible (BL, § 11, 3), Ac 17:15.†

τάσσω.long: (a) I assign, arrange, (b) I determine; mid: I appoint.
τάσσω.sd: to arrange in an orderly manner, i.e. assign or dispose (to a certain position or lot)
τάσσω.der: a prolonged form of a primary verb (which latter appears only in certain tenses);
τάσσω.as:
τάσσω
[in LXX chiefly for שׂוּם, also for צָוָה pi., נָתַן, etc. ;]
primarily, in military sense, then generally, to draw up in order, arrange in place, assign, appoint, order: c. dat. (acc) et inf. (Bl., § 72, 5), Ac 15:218:2 (διατ-, WH) 22:10; ἑαυτούς, I Co 16:15; pass., Mt 8:9 (T [WH], R, txt., om.), Lk 7:8, Ro 13:1; ὅσοι ἦσαν τεταγμένοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον (perh. in mid. sense; v. EGT and Page, in l.), Ac 13:48; mid., to appoint for oneself or by one's own authority, Mt 28:16, Ac 28:23.†

τρέμω.as:
τρέμω
to tremble, esp. with fear: Mk 5:33, Lk 8:47; c. ptcp. (in cl more freq. c. inf.), II Pe 2:10.†

ταλιθα.sd: the fresh, i.e. young girl; talitha (O maiden)

τηλαυγῶς.sd: in a far-shining manner, i.e. plainly
τηλαυγῶς.der: adverb from a compound of a derivative of G5056 (τέλος) and G827 (αὐγή);
τηλαυγῶς.as:
τηλαυγῶς
adv.
(< τῆλε, afar, + αὐγή, radiance), poët. and in late prose,
at a distance clearly: Mk 8:25 (WH, mg., δηλαυγῶς).†

τρίζω.sd: to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy)
τρίζω.as:
** τρίζω
[in Aq.: Am 2:13; Sm.: Is 38:14 * ;]
1. prop., of sounds by animals, to cry, chirp, etc.
2. Of other sounds, e.g., trans., τ. ὀδόντας, to gnash or grind the teeth: Mk 9:18.†

τρυμαλιά.sd: akin to the base of G5134 (τραῦμα), G5147 (τρίβος) and G5176 (τρώγω)); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye
τρυμαλιά.der: from a derivative of (to wear away;
τρυμαλιά.as:
† τρυμαλιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(< τρύω, to wear away), [in LXX: Je 13:4 (נָקִיק), etc. ;]
= τρύμη, a hole: τ. ῥαφίδος, eye of a needle, Mk 10:25.†
SYN.: τρῆμα, τρύπημα

Τιμαῖος.long: Timaeus, father of the blind beggar Bartimaeus.
Τιμαῖος.as:
Τιμαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. טִימַי (?), v. Zorell, s.v.),
Timæus: Mk 10:46.†

τρόμος.as:
τρόμος, -ου, ὁ
(< τρέμω), [in LXX for רִעָדָה, רַעַד, פַּחַד, etc. ;]
trembling, quaking, esp. from fear: Mk 16:8; φόβος κ. τ. (as in Ge 9:2, Ex 15:16, De 2:25, Is 19:16, al.), I Co 2:3, II Co 7:15, Eph 6:5, Phl 2:12.†

τάξις.long: order, (a) regular arrangement, (b) appointed succession, (c) position, rank.
τάξις.sd: regular arrangement, i.e. (in time) fixed succession (of rank or character), official dignity
τάξις.as:
τάξις, -εως, ἡ
(< τάσσω), [in LXX: Jb 38:12 (מָקוֹם), Ps 109 (110):4 (דִּבְרָה), II Mac 9:18, al. ;]
1.an arranging, hence, in military sense, disposition of an army, battle array (Thuc., al.).
2.arrangement, order (Plat., al): Lk 1:8.
3.due order: Col 2:5 (ICC, in l.); κατὰ τάξιν, I Co 14:40.
4.office, order (for exx., v. MM, xxiv): He 5:6(LXX), 106:207:11, 17(LXX).†

τελείωσις.sd: (the act) completion, i.e. (of prophecy) verification, or (of expiation) absolution
τελείωσις.as:
τελείωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< τελειόω), [in LXX chiefly for מִלֻּא, Ex 29:22, al. ;]
fulfilment, completion, perfection: Lk 1:45, He 7:11.†

ταπείνωσις.kj: humiliation, be made low, low estate, vile
ταπείνωσις.as:
ταπείνωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< ταπεινόω), [in LXX chiefly for עֳנִי ;]
abasement, humiliation, low estate: Lk 1:48, Ac 8:33(LXX), Phl 3:21, Ja 1:10 (Plat., Arist., and later writers).†

τρυγών.sd: akin to G5149 (τρίζω), but denoting a duller sound); a turtle-dove (as cooing)
τρυγών.as:
τρυγών, -όνος, ἡ
(< τρύζω, to murmur, coo), [in LXX for תּוֹר, תֹּר;]
a turtle-dove: Lk 2:24.†

τελειόω.long: (a) as a course, a race, or the like: I complete, finish (b) as of time or prediction: I accomplish, (c) I make perfect; pass: I am perfected.
τελειόω.sd: to complete, i.e. (literally) accomplish, or (figuratively) consummate (in character)
τελειόω.as:
τελειόω, -ῶ
(< τέλειος), [in LXX: Ex 29:9, Le 4:5, al. (τ. χεῖρας, מָלֵא pi.), II Ki 22:26, al. (תָּמַם), Wi 4:13, al. (cf. Westc., He., 64) ;]
1.bring to an end, finish, accomplish, fulfil: Jo 4:34, Ac 20:24; of time, Lk 2:43, Jo 5:3617:4; pass., ἡ γραφή, Jo 19:28.
2.to bring to maturity or completeness, to complete, perfect;
(a) of things: He 7:19, Ja 2:22, I Jo 2:54:12, 17 :
(b) of persons, in ethical and spiritual sense: He 2:109:910:1, 14; pass., Lk 13:32, Jo 17:23, Phl 3:12, He 5:97:2811:4012:23, I Jo 4:18 (for a different view of the meaning in He 2:10, al., v. Rendall, in l).†

Τιβέριος.long: Tiberius, the second Roman emperor (died A.D. 37).
Τιβέριος.sd: probably pertaining to the river Tiberis or Tiber; Tiberius, a Roman emperor

τετρααρχέω.g: I rule over as a tetrarch
τετρααρχέω.long: I rule over as a tetrarch.
τετρααρχέω.as:
† τετρααρχέω (Rec. τετραρχ-; v. WH, App., 145), -ῶ
(< τετραάρχης),
to be tetrarch: c. gen., Lk 3:1 (FlJ, BJ, iii, 10, 7).†

Τραχωνῖτις.long: Trachonitis, the north-east of the territory beyond Jordan.
Τραχωνῖτις.sd: rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria
Τραχωνῖτις.as:
Τραχωνῖτις, -ιδος, ἡ
(< τραχύς)
Trachonitis, a rough region S. of Damascus (in FlJ, sometimes ἡ Τ., sometimes ό Τράχων): ἡ Τ. χώρα, Lk 3:1.†

τραχύς.der: perhaps strengthened from the base of G4486 (ῥήγνυμι) (as if jagged by rents);
τραχύς.as:
τραχύς, -εῖα, -ύ
[in LXX: Is 40:4 (רֶכֶס), etc. ;]
rough: ὁδοί (Is, l.c.), Lk 3:5(LXX); τοποί (i.e. rocky), Ac 27:29.†

τρυγάω.der: from a derivative of (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry);
τρυγάω.as:
τρυγάω, -ῶ
[in LXX for קָצַר, בָּצַר, etc. ;]
to gather in: c. acc,
(a) of the fruit, Lk 6:44, Re 14:18;
(b) of that from which it is gathered, Re 14:19.†

τρυφή.der: from (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence);
τρυφή.as:
τρυφή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for עָדַן ;]
softness, daintiness, luxuriousness: Lk 7:25, II Pe 2:13.†

τελεσφορέω.sd: to be a bearer to completion (maturity), i.e. to ripen fruit (figuratively)
τελεσφορέω.der: from a compound of G5056 (τέλος) and G5342 (φέρω);
τελεσφορέω.as:
** τελεσφορέω, -ῶ
(< τέλος, φέρω) [in LXX: IV Mac 13:20 * ;]
(a) of plants, to bring fruit to perfection (Theophr.): Lk 8:14
(b) of females, to bear perfect offspring (Artemid.; IV Mac, l.c.).†

τραῦμα.sd: akin to the base of G2352 (θραύω), G5147 (τρίβος), G5149 (τρίζω), etc.); a wound
τραῦμα.as:
τραῦμα, -τος, τό
[in LXX for פָּצַע, חָלַל, etc. ;]
a wound: Lk 10:34.†

ταχέως.sd: briefly, i.e. (in time) speedily, or (in manner) rapidly
ταχέως.as:
ταχέως
(< ταχύς)
adv.,
[in LXX chiefly for מְהֵרָה and cognate forms ;]
quickly, hastily: Lk 14:2116:6, Jo 11:31, I Co 4:19, Phl 2:19, 24, II Ti 4:9; with suggestion of rashness, Ga 1:6, II Th 2:2, I Ti 5:22.†

τάχος.sd: a brief space (of time), i.e. (with G1722 (ἐν) prefixed) in haste
τάχος.as:
τάχος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of מָהַר ;]
swiftness, speed. Adverbially, ἐν τ. (= ταχέως), quickly, speedily, soon: Lk 18:8, Ac 12:722:1825:4, Ro 16:20, I Ti 3:14, Re 1:122:6.†

τρῆμα.as:
* τρῆμα, -τος, τό,
a perforation, hole: ῥαφίδος, Mt 19:24, WH, txt. βελόνης, Lk 18:25 (Aristoph., Plat., al.).†
SYN.: τρυμαλιά, τρύπημα

τετραπλοῦς.der: from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and a derivative of the base of G4118 (πλεῖστος);

τρίτον.sd: third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly
τρίτον.as:
τρίτος, -η, -ον
the third: Mt 22:26, Mk 12:2115:25, Lk 24:21, Ac 2:15, al.; τῇ τ. ἡμέρᾳ (i.e. the next day but one: Xen., al.; v. Field, Notes, 11 ff.), Mt 16:21, Lk 24:46, al.; substantively, acc. masc., τρίτον, a third (servant), Lk 20:12; neut., τὸ τ., c. gen., the third part of: Re 8:7-129:15, 1812:4. As adv., τὸ τ., the third time: Mk 14:41, Jo 21:17; anarth., τρίτον, a third time, Lk 23:22, Jo 21:14, II Co 12:1413:1; in enumerations, thirdly, I Co 12:28; ἐκ τ., a third time, Mt 26:44

τραυματίζω.as:
τραυματίζω
(< τραῦμα), [in LXX chiefly for חָלַל ;]
to wound: Lk 20:12, Ac 19:16.†

τοίνυν.long: indeed now, therefore, accordingly, well then.
τοίνυν.as:
τοί-νυν
an inferential particle,
[in LXX: Is 3:105:1327:4, Wi 1:118:9, a1. * ;]
accordingly, therefore: as in cl., after the first word in a sentence, I Co 9:26; acc to later usage, at the beginning, Lk 20:25, He 13:13.†

τυγχάνω.long: (a) gen: I obtain, (b) absol: I chance, happen; ordinary, everyday, it may chance, perhaps.
τυγχάνω.sd: akin to the base of G5088 (τίκτω) through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with G1487 (εἰ)), i.e. perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with G3756 (οὐ), extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were)
τυγχάνω.kj: be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh…self, + special
τυγχάνω.der: probably for an obsolete (for which the middle voice of another alternate (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses;
τυγχάνω.as:
τυγχάνω
[in LXX: De 19:5 (מָצָא), Jb 3:217:217:1, Pr 24:58 (30:23) (without definite Heb. equiv.), Wi 15:19, I Mac 11:42, III Mac 3:7, al. ;]
I. Trans.
1.to hit (opp. to ἁμαρτάνω, to miss the mark: Hom., Xen., al.).
2.to hit upon, light upon;
(a) of persons, to meet with, fall in with: absol., ptcp., ὁ τυχών, a chance person, anyone (Lat. quivis), οὐ τυχών, not common or ordinary, Ac 19:1128:2;
(b) of things, to reach, get, obtain: c. gen. rei. Lk 20:35, Ac 24:326:2227:3, II Ti 2:10He 8:611:35.
II. Intrans., to happen; of things, to happen, chance, befall: impers., εἰ τύχοι, it may be, perhaps, I Co 14:1015:37; so ptcp., τυχόν (old acc. absol.; v. M, Pr., 74), I Co 16:6
(cf. ἐν-, ὑπερ-εν-, ἐπι-, παρα-, συν-τυγχάνω).†

τετράμηνος.long: of four months, a period of four months.
τετράμηνος.der: neuter of a compound of G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G3376 (μήν);
τετράμηνος.as:
τετράμηνος, -ον
[in LXX (neut.): Jg 19:2 A 20:47 A (עַרְבָּעָה חֳדָשִׁים probably misspelled H702 אַרְבָּעָה) * ;]
of four months, four months; as subst., τ. (sc. ὥρα, but neut. in Rec.), Jo 4:35 (Thuc., al.).†

Τιβεριάς.long: Tiberias, a town in Galilee on the western border of the sea called after it.
Τιβεριάς.sd: Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine
Τιβεριάς.as:
Τιβεριάς, -άδος, ἡ
(< Τιβέριος),
Tiberias, a city of Galilee: Jo 6:23; θάλασσα τῆς, T., Jo 6:121:1 (cf Γεννησσαρέτ, Γαλιλαία).†

τεταρταῖος.long: of the fourth day, four days since.
τεταρταῖος.as:
τεταρταῖος, -α, -ον
(< τέταρτος), [in LXX: II Ki 3:4 A (רְבִיעִי) * ;]
of or on the fourth day: τ. εἶναι (Hdt., τ. γενέσθαι), to be four days dead, Jo 11:39.†

τυφλόω.long: I make blind, physically or mentally.
τυφλόω.sd: to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure
τυφλόω.as:
τυφλόω, -ῶ
(< τυφλός), [in LXX: Is 42:19 (עִוֵּר), To 7:7א, Wi 2:21א * ;]
to blind, make blind: metaph., Jo 12:40 (LXX, καμμύω), II Co 4:4, I Jo 2:11.†

τάχιον.sd: more swiftly, i.e. (in manner) more rapidly, or (in time) more speedily
τάχιον.der: neuter singular of the comparative of G5036 (ταχύς) (as adverb);

τεκνίον.sd: an infant, i.e. (plural figuratively) darlings (Christian converts)
τεκνίον.as:
† τεκνίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of τέκνον),
a little child: as a term of endearment, in voc. pl., Jo 13:33, Ga 4:19, I Jo 2:1, 12, 283:7, 184:45:21.†

τίτλος.as:
**† τίτλος, -ου, ὁ
(Lat. titulus), [in Aq., Sm., Th.: Je 21:4 * ;]
a title, inscription: Jo 19:19, 20 (in Christian Inscr., epitaph, v. MM. xxiv).†

τύπος.long: (originally: the mark of a blow, then a stamp struck by a die), (a) a figure; a copy, image, (b) a pattern, model, (c) a type, prefiguring something or somebody.
τύπος.sd: a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning)
τύπος.kj: en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print
τύπος.as:
τύπος, -ου, ὁ
(< τύπτω), [in LXX: Ex 25:39 (40) (תַּבְנִית), Am 5:26 (צֶלֶם), III Mac 3:30, IV Mac 6:19 * ;]
1. the mark of a blow: τῶν ἥλων, Jo 20:25.
2. An impression, impress, the stamp made by a die; hence, a figure, image: Ac 7:43(LXX).
3.form (Plat.): Ro 6:17; the sense or substance of a letter (III Mac, l.c.), Ac 23:25.
4.an example, pattern: Ac 7:44, He 8:6 (LXX); in ethical sense, Phl 3:17, I Th 1:7, II Th 3:9, I Ti 4:12, Tit 2:7, I Pe 5:3; in doctrinal sense, type (v. ICC, in l.), Ro 5:14.†
SYN.: v.s. ὑποτύπωσις

τεκμήριον.sd: a token (as defining a fact), i.e. criterion of certainty
τεκμήριον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a goal or fixed limit);
τεκμήριον.as:
** τεκμήριον, -ου, τό
(< τέκμαρ, a mark, sign), [in LXX: Wi 5:419:13, III Mac 3:24 * ;]
a sure sign, a positive proof: Ac 1:3 (for exx., v. MM, xxiv).†
SYN.: ἔνδειγμα, q.v

τήρησις.sd: a watching, i.e. (figuratively) observance, or (concretely) a prison
τήρησις.as:
** τήρησις, -εως, ἡ
(< τηρέω), [in LXX: Wi 6:18, (Si 35 (32):23), I Mac 5:18, II Mac 3:40, III Mac 5:44 * ;]
1.a watching, hence, imprisonment, ward (v. Deiss., BS, 267): Ac 4:35:18.
2.a keeping: τ. ἐντολῶν (cf. Sir, Wi, ll. c., and v. Westc. on I Jo 2:3.), I Co 7:19.†

τίμιος.sd: valuable, i.e. (objectively) costly, or (subjectively) honored, esteemed, or (figuratively) beloved
τίμιος.kj: dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation
τίμιος.as:
τίμιος, -α, -ον
(< τιμή), [in LXX chiefly for יָקָר ;]
valued, hence,
(a)precious, costly, highly valued: primarily, of money value, λίθος, Re 17:418:12, 1621:19; pl., I Co 3:12; compar., -ώτεφος, I Pe 1:7, Rec.; superl., -ώτατος, Re 18:1221:11; in extended sense, καρπός, Ja 5:7; αἷμα, I Pe 1:19; ἐπαγγέλματα, II Pe 1:4;
(b)held in honour, honoured, esteemed worthy: c. dat., Ac 5:34; ὁ γάμος, He 13:4; ψυχή, Ac 20:24 (where τ. is pleonastic, v. Page, in l.).†

τετρακόσιοι.as:
τετρακόσιοι, -αι, -α,
four hundred: Ac 5:367:6(LXX)13:20, Ga 3:17.†

Τίμων.long: Timon, one of the seven original deacons at Jerusalem.

τεσσερακονταετής.as:
** τεσσερακονταετής
(T, -έτης; Rec. τεσσαρ-, v. supr.), -ές
of forty years, forty years old: Ac 7:2313:18.†

Ταρσεύς.sd: a Tarsean, i.e. native of Tarsus
Ταρσεύς.as:
Ταρσεύς, -έως, ὁ
(< Ταρσός),
of Tarsus: Ac 9:1121:39.†

τεῖχος.long: a wall, especially of a city.
τεῖχος.sd: a wall (as formative of a house)
τεῖχος.der: akin to the base of G5088 (τίκτω);
τεῖχος.as:
τεῖχος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly for חוֹמָה ;]
a wall, esp. that about a town: Ac 9:25, II Co 11:33, He 11:30, Re 21:12-19 †

Ταρσός.long: Tarsus, the capital of the Roman province Cilicia.
Ταρσός.sd: Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor
Ταρσός.der: perhaps the same as (a flat basket);
Ταρσός.as:
Ταρσός, -οῦ
Tarsus, a city of Cilicia: Ac 9:3011:2522:3.†

Ταβιθά.long: antelope; Tabitha, a Christian woman at Joppa.
Ταβιθά.sd: the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female

τετράπους.as:
τετρά-πους, -ουν
[in LXX chiefly for בְּהֵמָה ;]
four-footed: of beasts, neut. pl., Ac 10:1211:6, Ro 1:23.†

τετράδιον.long: a quaternion, a group of four soldiers.
τετράδιον.sd: from G5064 (τέσσαρες)); a quaternion or squad (picket) of four Roman soldiers
τετράδιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a tetrad;
τετράδιον.as:
† τετράδιον, ου, τό
a quarternion, a group of four: στρατιωτῶν, Ac 12:4 (Philo).

τάραχος.as:
τάραχος, -ου, ὁ
(< ταράσσω), [in LXX for מְהוּמָה, etc. ;]
later form of ταραχή (Xen., al.; v. Thackeray, Gr., 159): Ac 12:1819:23.†

Τύριος.long: a Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre.
Τύριος.sd: a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus

τακτός.as:
τακτός, -ή, -όν
(< τάσσω), [in LXX: Jb 12:5 (שַׁאֲנָן) * ;]
ordered, fixed, stated: ἡμέρα, Ac 12:21,†

τροποφορέω.long: I endure the ways of, put up with.
τροποφορέω.as:
† τροπο-φορέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: De 1:31 B.l (נָשָׂא) * ;]
1.to bear another's manners (R, txt., suffered he their manners): c. acc pers., Ac 13:18 (Rec., WH, R, txt.; ἐτροφο-, T, R, mg.).
2. = τροφοφορέω (q.v.), (v. Kühner3, I, 276): Ac, l.c.†

Τιμόθεος.long: Timothy, a Christian of Lystra, helper of Paul.
Τιμόθεος.sd: dear to God; Timotheus, a Christian
Τιμόθεος.as:
Τιμόθεος, -ου, ὁ
Timothy: Ac 17:14, 1518:5, Ro 16:21, al.

Τρῳάς.long: Troas, a harbor city of Mysia.
Τρῳάς.sd: the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor
Τρῳάς.as:
Τρῳάς (Rec. Τρω-), -άδος, ἡ
Troas, a city near the Hellespont: Ac 16:8, 1120:5, 6, II Co 2:12, II Ti 4:13.†

τέχνη.sd: art (as productive), i.e. (specially), a trade, or (generally) skill
τέχνη.as:
τέχνη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX for חׇכְמָה, מַעֲשֶׂה, עֲבֹדָה ;]
art, craft, trade: Ac 17:2918:3, Re 18:22 (WH, R, mg., om.).†

Τίτιος.as:
Τίτιος, -ου, ὁ,
Titius, surnamed Justus: Ac 18:7, T, WH (RV., Τίτος).†

Τύραννος.long: Tyrannus, an inhabitant of Ephesus, probably a rhetorician.
Τύραννος.der: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of G2962 (κύριος);

τεχνίτης.as:
τεχνίτης, -ου, ὁ
(< τέχνη), [in LXX for חָרָשׁ, etc. ;]
a craftsman, artificer: Ac 19:24, 38, Re 18:22; of God (Wi 13:1), He 11:10.†
SYN.: δημιουργός, q.v., and cf. Tr., Syn., § cv

Τυχικός.long: Tychicus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia.
Τυχικός.sd: fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian
Τυχικός.as:
Τύχικος, (T, Rec., Τυχικός), -ου, ὁ
Tychicus: Ac 20:4, Eph 6:21, Col 4:7, II Ti 4:12, Tit 3:12.†

Τρόφιμος.long: Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia.
Τρόφιμος.as:
Τρόφιμος, -ου, ὁ
Trophimus: Ac 20:421:29, II Ti 4:20.†

τρίστεγον.g: having three stories, the third story
τρίστεγον.long: having three stories; subst: the third story.
τρίστεγον.der: neuter of a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G4721 (στέγη) as noun;
τρίστεγον.as:
**† τρίστεγος, -ον (τρεῖς, στέγη)
[in Sm.: Ge 6:17(16), Ez 42:6 * ;]
of three stories: τὸ τ. (sc. ὄκημα),
the third story, Ac 20:9 (Dion., FlJ, al.).†

ταπεινοφροσύνη.kj: humbleness of mind, humility (of mind, loneliness (of mind)
ταπεινοφροσύνη.der: from a compound of G5011 (ταπεινός) and the base of G5424 (φρήν);
ταπεινοφροσύνη.as:
*† ταπεινοφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(< ταπεινόφρων)
lowliness of mind, humility: Ac 20:19, Eph 4:2, Phl 2:3, Col 3:12, I Pe 5:5; of a false humility, Col 2:18, 23 (rare outside of NT, but found in bad sense in FlJ, BJ, iv, 9, 2; also in Epictet., v. Tr., Syn., § xlii).†

τριετία.der: from a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G2094 (ἔτος);
τριετία.as:
* τριετία, -ας, ἡ
(< τρεῖς, ἔτος),
a period of three years: Ac 20:31.†

τιμωρέω.sd: properly, to protect one's honor, i.e. to avenge (inflict a penalty)
τιμωρέω.der: from a comparative of G5092 (τιμή) and ouros (a guard);
τιμωρέω.as:
τιμωρέω, -ῶ
(< τιμή + οὖρος, a guardian) [in LXX: Ez 5:1714:15 (שָׁכֹל pi), Wi 12:2018:8, al. ;]
1.to help.
2.to avenge; mid., to avenge oneself on, punish (Hdt., Eur., al): act, in this sense, Ac 22:526:11 (v. MM, xxiv).†

τοῖχος.as:
τοῖχος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for קִיר ;]
a wall, esp. of a house: fig., Ac 23:3 (cf. τεῖχος).†

Τέρτυλλος.long: Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor of Paul at Caesarea.

τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος.der: from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G2532 (καί) and G1182 (δέκατος);

Τρεῖς.as:
τρεῖς, οἱ, αἱ, τρία, τά
three: Mt 12:40, al.; μετὰ τ. ἡμέρας = τῇ τρίτῃ ἡ., Mk 10:34, al. (cf. Field, Notes, 11 ff.)

Ταβέρνη.long: taverns; Three Taverns, the name of a village or town on the Appian Way, about thirty-three miles from Rome.

ταλαιπωρία.as:
ταλαιπωρία, -ας, ἡ
(< ταλαίπωρος) [in LXX chiefly for שֹׁד ;]
1.hard work (Hippocr.).
2.hardship, suffering, distress: Ro 3:16(LXX) pl., Ja 5:1 (v. B1., § 32, 6; WM, 220; Swete, Mk., 153).
(Hdt., Thuc., al.; and cf. MM, xxiv.)†

τάχα.der: as if neuter plural of G5036 (ταχύς) (adverbially);
τάχα.as:
** τάχα
(< ταχύς),
adv.,
[in LXX: Wi 13:614:19 * ;]
(a) (chiefly poët.), quickly, presently;
(b)perhaps: Ro 5:7, Phm 15.†

ταλαίπωρος.der: from the base of G5007 (τάλαντον) and a derivative of the base of G3984 (πεῖρα);
ταλαίπωρος.as:
ταλαίπωρος, -ον
[in LXX: Ps 136 (137):8 (שָׁדַד), Is 33:1 (ποιεῖν τ., שָׁדַד), To 13:10, Wi 3:11, al. ;]
distressed, miserable, wretched: Ro 7:24, Re 3:17.†

τολμηρότερον.long: more boldly, more freely, with more confidence.
τολμηρότερον.sd: more daringly, i.e. with greater confidence than otherwise
τολμηρότερον.der: neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of 5111 (as adverb);
τολμηρότερον.as:
* τολμηρῶς
adv.,
(< τολμηρός, bold, daring),
boldly: compar., -ότερως (T, Rec. -ότερον), Ro 15:15.†

Τρύφαινα.long: Tryphaena, a Christian woman in Rome.
Τρύφαινα.as:
Τρύφαινα, -ης, ἡ
Tryphæna: Ro 16:12 (v. Lft., Phl., 175 f.; MM, xxv).†

Τρυφῶσα.long: Tryphosa, a Christian woman in Rome, perhaps a sister of Tryphaena.
Τρυφῶσα.as:
Τρυφῶσα, -ης, ἡ, ς, ἡ
Tryphosa: Ro 16:12 (v. Lft., Phl., 175 f.).†

Τέρτιος.long: Tertius, who wrote the Epistle to the Romans at Paul's dictation.

τυπικῶς.as:
*† τυπικῶς,
adv.,
(< τύπος),
(a)typically (Greg. Naz.) ,̓
(b)by way of example: I Co 10:11.†

τάγμα.sd: something orderly in arrangement (a troop), i.e. (figuratively) a series or succession
τάγμα.as:
τάγμα, -τος, τό
(< τάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for דֶּגֶל, also for חַיָּה, רַגְלִי ;]
that which has been arranged or placed in order; esp. as military term, a company, troop, division, rank: metaph., I Co 15:23 (v. ICC, in l.).†

τηλικοῦτος.sd: such as this, i.e. (in (figurative) magnitude) so vast
τηλικοῦτος.der: from a compound of G3588 (ὁ) with G2245 (ἡλίκος) and G3778 (οὗτος);
τηλικοῦτος.as:
* τηλικοῦτος, -αύτη, -οῦτο
(altern. of τηλικόσδε, -ήδε, -όνδε, strength­ened form of τηλίκος), [in LXX: II Mac 12:3, III Mac 3:9, IV Mac 16:4 * ;]
1. of persons,
(a)of such an age, so old;
(b)so young.
2. Of things, so great: II Co 1:10, He 2:3, Ja 3:4, Re 16:18.†

τοὐναντίον.long: on the contrary, on the other hand.
τοὐναντίον.der: contraction for the neuter of G3588 (ὁ) and G1726 (ἐναντίον);
τοὐναντίον.as:
τοὐναντίον
by crasis for τὸ ἐνανίον, neut. acc, used adverbially, on the contrary, contrariwise: II Co 2:7, Ga 2:7, I Pe 3:9.†

Τίτος.long: Titus, a Greek Christian, helper of Paul, perhaps also brother of Luke.
Τίτος.der: of Latin origin but uncertain significance;
Τίτος.as:
Τίτος, -ου, ὁ
Titus;
1. St. Paul's disciple and companion: II Co 2:137:6, 13, 148:6, 16, 2312:18, Ga 2:1, 3, II Ti 4:10, Tit 1:4, subscr., Rec. (Τῖτος).
2. One surnamed Justus: Ac 18:7, RV (T, WH, Τίτιος).†

τελειότης.as:
τελειότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< τέλειος), [in LXX: Jg 9:16, 19 (תָּמִים), Pr 11:3 (תֻּמָּה), Wi 6:1512:17, Je 2:2 * ;]
perfection, completeness: Col 3:14, He 6:1

τροφός.as:
τροφός, -οῦ, ἡ
(< τρέφω), [in LXX: Ge 35:8, IV Ki 11:2, II Ch 22:11Is 49:23 (מֵינֶקֶת) * ;]
a nurse: I Th 2:7.†

τοιγαροῦν.long: consequently, therefore, well then, so then.
τοιγαροῦν.der: from G5104 (τοί) and G1063 (γάρ) and G3767 (οὖν);
τοιγαροῦν.as:
τοι-γαρ-οῦν
an inferential particle,
[in LXX: Jb 22:1024:22 (עַל־כֵּך), Si 41:16, al. ;]
wherefore then, so therefore: I Th 4:8, He 12:1 (Hdt., Plat., al.).†

τίνω.sd: to pay a price, i.e. as a penalty
τίνω.der: strengthened for a primary (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses);
τίνω.as:
τίνω
[in LXX: Pr 27:12 (τ. ζημίαν, for עָנַשׁ ni.), etc. ;]
to pay: τ. δίκην (cf. Pr, l.c.), to pay penalty, II Th 1:9 (v. M, Th., in l.).†

τεκνογονία.long: child bearing, the rearing of a family.
τεκνογονία.sd: childbirth (parentage), i.e. (by implication) maternity (the performance of maternal duties)

τυφόομαι.long: I puff up, make haughty; pass: I am puffed up, am haughty.
τυφόομαι.sd: to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit
τυφόομαι.kj: high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud
τυφόομαι.as:
* τυφόω, -ῶ
(< τῦφος, smoke; metaph., conceit),
prop., to wrap in smoke; used only metaph., to puff up, becloud with pride: pass., I Ti 3:66:4, II Ti 3:4 (Dem., Arist., al.).†

τεκνοτροφέω.long: I bring up children, rear young.
τεκνοτροφέω.sd: to be a childrearer, i.e. fulfil the duties of a female parent
τεκνοτροφέω.der: from a compound of G5043 (τέκνον) and G5142 (τρέφω);
τεκνοτροφέω.as:
* τεκνο-τροφέω, -ῶ
to rear young (of bees, Arist.),
to bring up children: I Ti 5:10.†

τεκνογονέω.long: I bear children, beget, rear a family.
τεκνογονέω.sd: to be a child-bearer, i.e. parent (mother)
τεκνογονέω.der: from a compound of G5043 (τέκνον) and the base of G1096 (γίνομαι);
τεκνογονέω.as:
*† τεκνογονέω, -ῶ
to beget or bear children: I Ti 5:14 (Anthol.).†

τομώτερος.sd: more comprehensive or decisive than G2875 (κόπτω), as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen
τομώτερος.der: comparative of a derivative of the primary (to cut;
τομώτερος.as:
* τομός, -ή, -όν
(< τέμνω),
sharp: compar., -ώτερος, metaph., He 4:12.†

τραχηλίζομαι.g: I am laid bare, laid open
τραχηλίζομαι.long: I am laid bare, laid open.
τραχηλίζομαι.sd: to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare)
τραχηλίζομαι.as:
† τραχηλίζω
(< τράχηλος),
prop., of wrestlers,
to take by the throat, hence (Philo), to prostrate, overthrow. Metaph., but in what sense and from what age it is doubtful (v. Westc., Rendall, on He, l.c.; DB, iii, 625n), τραχηλισμένα, laid open (RV, Westc.; downcast, Rendall): He 4:13.†

τράγος.as:
τράγος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for עַתּוּד, also for צָפִיר, תַּיִשׁ ;]
a he-goat: He 9:12, 13, 1910:4.†

τιμωρία.as:
τιμωρία, -ας, ἡ
(< τιμωρέω), [in LXX: Pr 24:22 (פִּיד), etc. ;]
1.help, assistance.
2.vengeance, punishment: He 10:29.†
SYN.: κόλασις, q.v., and cf. MM, xxiv

τρίμηνον.der: neuter of a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G3376 (μήν) as noun;
τρίμηνον.as:
τρίμηνος, -ον
(< τρεῖς, μήν) [in LXX (neut.): Ge 38:24, IV Ki 23:31 B 24:8, II Ch 36:2, 9 (חֳדָשִׁים שָׁלוֹשׁ) * ;]
of three months; as subst., τὸ τ. (= cl. ἡ τ.), a space of three months (Polyb., al.; LXX): He 11:23.†

τυμπανίζω.g: I torture, break on the wheel
τυμπανίζω.long: I torture, break on the wheel, beat to death.
τυμπανίζω.sd: to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death
τυμπανίζω.der: from a derivative of G5180 (τύπτω) (meaning a drum, "tympanum");
τυμπανίζω.as:
τυμπανίζω
(< τύμπανον, a kettle-drum), [in LXX: I Ki 21:13 (14) (תָּוָה pi?) * ;]
1.to beat a drum.
2.to torture by beating, beat to death (cf. Westc. on He, l.c.): pass., He 11:35.†

τελειωτής.as:
τελειωτής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< τελειόω),
a consummator, finisher: He 12:2 (nowhere else).†

τροχιά.g: the track of a wheel, a path
τροχιά.long: the track of a wheel, a path.
τροχιά.sd: a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct
τροχιά.as:
τροχιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(< τροχός), [in LXX: Pr 2:154:11, 26, 275:6, 21 (מַעְגָּל), Ez 27:19 A* ;]
the track of a wheel, hence, a track, path: fig., He 12:13(LXX) †

τροπή.der: from an apparently primary to turn;
τροπή.as:
τροπή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< τρέπω), [in LXX: De 33:14, Jb 38:33, Wi 7:18, al. ;]
a turning: esp. of the revolution of heavenly bodies, fig., Ja 1:17 (v.s. ἀποσκίασμα).†

τροχός.sd: a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects
τροχός.as:
τροχός, -οῦ, τό
(< τρέχω), [in LXX chiefly for אוֹפָן ;]
a wheel: Ja 3:6 (v. Mayor, Hort, in l.).†

ταλαιπωρέω.long: I endure severe hardship, am harassed, complain.
ταλαιπωρέω.sd: to be wretched, i.e. realize one's own misery
ταλαιπωρέω.as:
ταλαιπωρέω, -ῶ
(< ταλαίπωρος), [in LXX Chiefly for שָׁדַד pu. ;]
1.to do hard labour, suffer hardship or distress: Ja 4:9.
2. In cl. occasionally trans., to weary, distress (so Ps 16 (17):9, Is 33:1).†

τρυφάω.long: I live a luxurious life, live self-indulgently.
τρυφάω.as:
τρυφάω, -ῶ
(< τρυφή), [in LXX: Ne 9:25 (עָדַן hithp.), Is 66:11 (עָנַג hithp.), Si 14:4 * ;]
to live daintily, luxuriously, to fare sumptuously: Ja 5:5 (cf. ἐν-τρυφάω).†
SYN.: σπαταλάω (q.v.), στρηνιάω

τελείως.as:
** τελείως
(< τέλειος),
adv.,
[in LXX: Jth 11:6, II Mac 12:42, III Mac 3:267:22, R* ;]
completely, perfectly: I Pe 1:13.†

ταπεινόφρων.as:
† ταπεινόφρων, -ον
(< ταπεινός, φρήν), [in LXX: Pr 29:23 (רוּחַשָׁפָל)* ;]
humble-minded: I Pe 3:8 (in bad sense, Plut., 2, 336 E, cf. Deiss., LAE, 723).†

ταχινός.as:
ταχινός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX: Pr 1:16, Hb 1:6, Is 59:7 (מָהַר), Wi 13:2, Si 11:2218:26 * ;]
poët. and late for ταχύς, swift: of swift approach, II Pe 1:142:1.†

τοιόσδε.long: of this kind, such, such as follows.
τοιόσδε.der: (including the other inflections); from a derivative of 5104 and G1161 (δέ);

ταρταρόω.long: I thrust down to Tartarus or Gehenna.
ταρταρόω.as:
*† ταρταρόω, -ῶ
(< Τάρταρος, a Greek name for the underworld, esp. the abode of the damned),
to cast into hell: II Pe 2:4 (v. Mayor, in l.).†

τεφρόω.long: I reduce to ashes, consume, destroy.
τεφρόω.as:
τεφρόω, -ῶ
(< τέφρα, ashes; Wi 2:3, al.),
to burn to ashes: II Pe 2:6.†

τολμητής.as:
* τολμητής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< τολμάω),
a bold, daring man: II Pe 2:10 (Thuc.).†

τήκομαι.long: I make liquid; pass: I melt (away).
τήκομαι.as:
τήκω
[in LXX for מָסַס ni., מָקַק ni., מוּג ni., etc. ;]
trans.,
to melt, melt down; pass., to melt, melt away: II Pe 3:12.†

τόξον.sd: a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric)
τόξον.as:
τόξον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for קֶשֶׁת ;]
a bow: Re 6:2.†

τρίχινος.as:
τρίχινος, -η, -ον
(< θρίξ), [in LXX: Za 13:4 (שֵׂעָר), Ex 26:7 * ;]
of hair: στόκος, Re 6:12 (Xen., Plat., al.).†

ταλαντιαῖος.as:
* ταλαντιαῖος, -α, -ον
(< τάλαντον),
(a)worth a talent;
(b)of a talent's weight: Re 16:21.†

τιμιότης.as:
* τιμιότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< τίμιος),
preciousness, worth: Re 18:19 (cf. Hort on τιμή, I Pe 2:7).†

τετράγωνος.as:
τετράγωνος, -ον
(< τετρα-, v. supr., + γωνία), [in LXX for רָבוּעַ and cogn. forms ;]
square: Re 21:16 (Hdt., Plat., al.).†

τοπάζιον.sd: of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite
τοπάζιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of (a "topaz";
τοπάζιον.as:
† τοπάζιον, -ου, τό
(and τόπαζος, ὁ), [in LXX: Ex 28:1735:17 (Ex 39:10), Jb 28:19, Ez 28:13 (פִּטְדָה), Ps 118 (119):127 (פָּז)* ;]
topaz: Re 21:20 (v. Swete, in l.).†
